'Establishing Discipline and Accountability in the Environmental Review and Permitting Process for Infrastructure Projects'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the purpose and policy (secs. 1-2), definitions (sec. 3), a Cross-Agency Priority Goal and performance accountability system (sec. 4), process enhancements - 'One Federal Decision', permitting timetables, the Dashboard, EO 13766 implementation, CEQ and FPISC duties, energy corridors and an Interior reorganization strategy (sec. 5) - the revocation of EO 13690 (sec. 6) and general provisions (sec. 7). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are condition (sec. 5(b)(ii)-(iii), 5(c), 5(d), 5(f)(i), 7(b)), fixed_term (sec. 4(b)) and until_event (sec. 5(b)(iv)). The fixed_term is the '180 days of the establishment of the CAP Goal, or such longer period as determined by the Director of OMB' for OMB's accountability guidance: a deadline for performing a command, not an end. The until_event is 'until the design of a project has sufficiently advanced': a rule about when a project's timetable dates may be left blank, not an end. The order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(b) says 'Executive Order 13807 ... is hereby revoked'; whole scope, no exception (the only sec. 7 exception is EO 13834); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out as ends or amendments: 'target provision not located: EO:13766' (EO 13807 sec. 5(d) implements EO 13766 and redirects the CEQ Chairman's secs. 2-3 responsibilities; EO 13766 was revoked by EO 13990 sec. 7(a) the same day: nothing earlier); 'EO:13781' (sec. 5(h) tells OMB to fold Interior's strategy into the plan under EO 13781: a coordination cross-reference); 'EO:13817' (sec. 4(b) of EO 13817 tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy consistently with EO 13807: a cross-reference). Other actor provision ACT:EO:13807>EO:14030: EO 14030 sec. 5(e) does not revoke EO 13807 (it narrates that EO 13807 had revoked EO 13690 and reinstates EO 13690); it is attached as a later event on sec6 only. EO 13921 sec. 6(a) (2020-05-07; effective on signing, no effective-date wording) tells agencies reviewing aquaculture projects to 'use the ''One Federal Decision'' process enhancements described in section 5(b) of Executive Order 13807': an incorporation by reference of sec. 5(b), not an amendment, suspension or revocation of EO 13807, so no later event is attached (EO 13921 is also not among the dossier's evidence records, so it could not be attached); EO 14276 (2025-04-17, 90 FR 16993) says EO 13921 'remains in effect', and the use of the process for aquaculture continues under EO 13921 itself after EO 13807's revocation - see savings_residuals. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts finds EO 13807 named only in EO 13817, 13921, 13990 and 14030, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement of EO 13807 itself is recorded. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but do not name EO 13807 or reinstate it, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Inventory: the dossier's 52 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 7(c). Inventory correction: the dossier mislabels sub-items with 'dup2/dup3/dup4' suffixes and omits lettered parents, and its 25-character clause 'sec5-b' ('(b) One Federal Decision.') is too short for the claim-checker's quotation test; inventory_overrides keep every dossier span, rename the scopes and merge sec5-b into the adjacent Sec. 5(b)(i) (51 spans, no gap or overlap). Some dossier spans carry the FR running header or VerDate footer from a page break. Savings: see savings_residuals (continuing_independent, S1 prefill resolved).","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[{"file_sha256":"5f1616fae97c0b04ff5849ae2cc8f2437ee95014d2c366ad1ce2d1a1a1ca532e","path":"research/excavator/astra-production-2026-10-24/b01/complete-v1/receipts/research/valla/pilot-2026-10-20/METHOD_REVIEWS.jsonl","pointer":"line:5","review_kind":"independent_ai_method_review","scope":"The clock depends on CAP-goal establishment and may be extended. rch_rationale":"The section 2(b). The originals contain no sunset, completed assignment, or independent command outside those host-rule amendments. Probation and objection conditions govern recurring application rather than ending the entire order. EO 8707 and EO 8423 are later amendments, with before-and-after text retained. The earlier ACT commentary that EO 8707 ended EO 8179 item 2 is reconsidered under the owner's October 21 strike-and-insert ruling, which continues the amended clause.\n\nThe full text and operative pages of EO 9830 were examined. Its opening May 1, 1947 effective date governs Parts I, II and III. Part II replaces the Civil Service Rules, and Part III expressly names both target orders and their original dates without a savings qualification. Every original footprint therefore ends on May 1, 1947 under the owner's October 21 unnamed-instruments convention. This is the convention's named endpoint, not a claim that no substantive application changed earlier. The earlier War Service Regulations and 1946 temporary regulations are pinned and expressly disclosed as candidate earlier changes. The 1942 list does not include Rule XI. The 1946 effective-date qualification is preserved rather than converted to an unsupported exact date.\n\nEO 9691 and temporary regulation 27.16(g) protect acquired rights, tenure and benefits. These are separately analyzed as saved acts and successor authority, not silently erased or treated as current authority under the revoked target orders. No independent target command or present application of the old target terms was identified in the bounded later-source, host-rule, savings and revival checks. The U.S. Code machine search reaches October 9 only; it is not the sole bridge to the October 14, 2026 cutoff. No held source shows whether the permission carried over to the successor (Social Security Administration) personnel until EO 11408's revocation on 1968-04-25 or lapsed in 1946 for want of its named agency, so first_end and whole_order_end are left open; EO 11408 is recorded as a later event."],"research_rationale":"Executive Order 8399 (official Federal Register text, 5 FR 1607, PDF pages 1-1, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits (1) Social Security Board officers and employees, on the Board's recommendation and the Federal Security Administrator's approval, to hold state, territorial and municipal office in cooperative work with the Board, and (2) state, territorial and municipal officers in such work to serve under the Board. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. The order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. However, the order names the Social Security Board, which was abolished in 1946, so an earlier cessation is possible and the first end is not asserted (see gap); EO 11408's revocation is recorded as a later event. Partial claim: original text, clause inventory, savings and later-source search are asserted; the ending is not. The held text is a reading-order extract in which the order's body is interrupted by the issue's contents column, masthead and the first lines of an unrelated Department of Agriculture marketing order, and its signature block is printed after that marketing text. Inventory correction: the dossier inventory (15 clauses starting at character 3279 and running to 12012) is not the order; it takes page furniture and the marketing order for clauses. The order has two operative paragraphs: (1) the tract of about 9,300 acres lying within the described Turnagain Arm boundaries is excluded from the Chugach National Forest, under the act of June 4, 1897; (2) under the act of March 12, 1914 (38 Stat. 305, 307) the same tract is withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry or other disposition and reserved for townsite purposes in connection with the construction and operation of railroad lines. I replaced the inventory with two exact spans of the held text: characters 3279 to 9328 (paragraph 1, which includes the page furniture that falls inside the boundary description) and 9329 to 9781 (paragraph 2). The numeral 9,300 acres closes the first span. Ending: Public Land Order 835 (17 FR 4948, held page extract jobs/selden-fr-acting/output/texts/FR_17_4948.txt, sha256 7d4ce09b9fbae911cb373617d34b55faf1822e143bce9b331be66ee80faa8077, bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-835-EO-8480) is headed Revocation of Executive Order No. 8480 of July 12, 1940 and its paragraph 1 revokes the order, with a proviso that the revocation does not return any of the lands to national forest status; it is signed by the Secretary of the Interior on May 23, 1952 (F.R. Doc. 52-5945, filed 1952-05-29). Earlier partial events: Public Land Order 571 (14 FR 1175, held page extract FR_14_1175.txt, sha256 2cff211ecf5ccd6926fe8639dbb569489f6bda025e32a7cd71927912502d0a6e; bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-571-EO-8480) set two parcels aside for The Alaska Railroad and modified the order to the extent necessary; Public Land Order 686 (15 FR 7799, held page extract FR_15_7799.txt, sha256 ab0a69c8d7d98b4eea38e06b49f6d48a977c2e1fac1f14672a9b3a9f1ac8db34; bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-686-EO-8480) revoked the order only as to Tract No. 1 (Portage air-navigation site). Selden leads: used the three Federal Register page leads (PLO 571, 686, 835), each read in full; used the statute lead 30 Stat. 11 only as the authority the order itself cites for paragraph 1 (the act of June 4, 1897, 30 Stat. 11, 36; the Act's text was not read for this claim); rejected the statute leads 49 Stat. 115, 49 Stat. 500, 49 Stat. 750, 50 Stat. 246 and 50 Stat. 522, which are artifacts of the neighbouring orders and Federal Register furniture on the same pages; read 38 Stat. 305 (the Alaska Railroad act, authority for paragraph 2) and found nothing ending a withdrawal before 1952. The 1994-on full-text search returned 0 hits. Without the three PLO texts neither the ending nor the counterevidence could be done; the inventory correction needed only the original. Federal Register full-text search (federalregister.gov API v1, 1994 on) for the order number, limited to documents published from January 1994 through 14 October 2026, checked 2026-11-06: 0 hits, complete; the search covers 1994 on only and absence of a hit is bounded to that query.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Held texts that cite 8480 by number: the bounded search found three, Public Land Orders 571, 686 and 835. Only 835 revokes the order in full. Public Land Order 571 modifies the order and Public Land Order 686 revokes it only as to Tract No. 1; Public Land Order 686 also says that as to Tract No. 2 it takes precedence over, but does not modify, the order as modified by Public Land Order 571, so the order was still in force in part in 1950. Public Land Order 835 revokes the order as an existing instrument in 1952, which excludes any earlier whole-order end. The order has no duration term. I read the whole authority act (38 Stat. 305 to 307, held in the packet as SUPPLEMENT:stat-38-Stat-305-EO-8480): it authorizes the President to withdraw and dispose of town-site areas along the proposed railroad lines and contains no expiry of that authority, so no statutory sunset ended the withdrawal before 1952. The first paragraph (the exclusion from the forest) was performed on issue, so its first end is the order date.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Two independent commands: the exclusion from the Chugach National Forest (a one-time act that took effect when the order issued) and the withdrawal and reservation for townsite purposes (continuing until revoked). No report, duty or recurring obligation. The exclusion's surviving consequence is preserved by the proviso in Public Land Order 835, paragraph 1, and is a consequence, not a continuing command of the order.\",\"savings_check\":\"Savings searched in the order and in Public Land Orders 571, 686 and 835 as read in full. Residual effects are the national forest exclusion preserved by the proviso, the railroad reserve and the new withdrawals made by Public Land Order 835; each rests on a later instrument.\",\"scope_check\":\"Public Land Order 835 names the order in its heading and in paragraph 1 and revokes it in full, for the whole tract, including paragraph 2's withdrawal and reservation; it does not name paragraph 1's exclusion separately but its proviso says the revocation does not return the lands to national forest status, so it preserves rather than ends the exclusion. For that reason the exclusion clause is ended by performance, not by the public land order. Public Land Orders 571 and 686 are partial and are recorded as later events of paragraph 2 and necessary for \nthis purpose, see that such price increases \ndo not cause price increases at later levels \nof production or distribution, and (2) \nimprove and tighten price controls in \nthose fields which are important in rela­\ntion to production costs or the cost of \nliving in which in their judgment the \ncontrols have heretofore been insuffi­\nciently effective. ..\nrv\n1.","With respect to violations, rights ac­\ncrued, liabilities incurred, or appeals \ntaken, prior to said date, under War Food \nOrder No. 75-2, as amended, all provi­\nsions of said order shall be deemed to \nremain in full force for the purpose of \nsustaining any proper suit, action, or \nother proceeding with respect to any \nsuch violation, right, liability, or appeal.","With respect to violations, rights \naccrued, liabilities incurred, or appeals \ntaken, prior to said date, under War Food \nOrder No. 75-3, all provisions of said or­\nder shall, be deemed to remain in full \nforce for the purpose of sustaining any \nproper suit, action, or'other proceeding \nwith respect to any such violation, right, \nliability, or appeal.","With \nrespect to violations, rights accrued, lia­\nbilities incurred, or appeals taken, prior \nto said date, under War Food Order No. \n75-4, as amended, all provisions of said \nordér shall be deemed to remain in full \nforce for the purpose of sustaining any \nproper suit, action, or other proceeding \nWith respect to any such-violation, right, \nliability, or appeal.","Department Circular No. 653, Second \nRevision, dated August 31, 1943, as sup­\nplemented June 7, 1944, fixing the terms \nand governing the issue of United States \nSavings Bonds of Series E, currently \ndesignated War Savings Bonds, is hereby \nfurther supplemented, as follows:\n1 .","The provisions of \nsaid Circular No. 653, Second Revision, \nand the regulations governing savings \nbonds shall extend to bonds of Series E \nin the denomination of $200.\n2.","Such termination on October  \n1, 1945 of the order and directions referred  \nto above shall not affect any liabilities in­\ncurred for violation of any of such orders or  \ndirections, or of actions taken by the War  \nProduction Board under them."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1945-08-18","target_id":"EO:9301","verb":"revoke"}

{"actor_id":"EO:9600","char_end":90510,"char_start":89760,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2784,"char_start":2309,"text":"To assist in the maximum produc­\ntion of goods and services required to \nmeet domestic and foreign needs, (1) by \nassuring assistance in making available \nmaterials and supplies required for the \nproduction of such goods and services;\n(2) by providing assistance to the con­\nversion and utilization of war plants and \nfacilities, both privately and publicly \nowned; and (3) by providing effective \njob placement assistance to war workers \nand returning service men and women."},{"char_end":4492,"char_start":3495,"text":"The departments and agencies of \nthe Government shall take vigorous, con­\ncerted and uniform action toward these \nends and pursuant to this Order, under \nthe guidance and direction of the Direc­\ntor of War Mobilization and Recon­\nversion.\nn\nDuring the transition to a free econ­\nomy, the Secretary of Agriculture, the \nFederal Loan Administrator, and the Di­\nrector of Economic Stabilization shall \nnot only take all measures required by \nlaw to support prices but shall take such \nfurther measures authorized by law as \nmay be necessary to prevent any collapse \nof values or discouragement of the full \nand effective use of productive resources.\nn i\nThe Price Administrator, and in the \nexercise of his price responsibilities un­\nder the law the Secretary of Agriculture, \nshall, subject to such directives provided \nfor by law as may be issued by the Eco­\nnomic Stabilization Director, take all \nnecessary steps to assure that the cost \nof living and the general level of prices \nshall not rise."},{"char_end":4882,"char_start":4493,"text":"Subject to such author­\nity, the Price Administrator and, in the \nexercise of his price responsibilities un­\nder the law, the Secretary of Agricul­\nture, are authorized to make such adjust­\nments in existing price controls as are \nnecessary to remove gross inequities or to \ncorrect maladjustments or inequities \nwhich would interfere with the effective \ntransition to a peacetime economy."},{"char_end":23412,"char_start":21513,"text":"Part 907—Governing employ­\nment stabilization pro*\ngrams__________________- 10106\nChapter IX \nagency is hereby authorized to approve, \nwithout regard to the limitations con­\ntained in any other orders or directives, \nsuch increases as may be necessary to \ncorrect maladjustments or Roosevelt; 8 FR 1825, issue of Thursday, February 11, 1943), read in full in the held Federal Register text, declares that \"For the duration of the war\" no plant or place of employment is deemed to make the most effective use of manpower if its minimum workweek is under 48 hours (section 1, inside the lead row of the machine inventory), directs agencies to require contractors to comply (2), authorizes the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission to interpret the order and issue policies, directives and regulations and to set a different workweek in particular cases (3), requires agencies to comply (4) and states that the order is not to supersede other hours or wage laws (5). EO 9607 (August 30, 1945), held Federal Register text, revokes it by number in one sentence. The phrase \"For the duration of the war\" is an own-terms condition; no held instrument or source fixes a legal end of the war before August 30, 1945, and EO 9607 revokes the order outright without reciting that it had lapsed, so the first end is the express revocation.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"No earlier end is held. Own terms: section 1 begins \\\"For the duration of the war\\\", which ends on a legal event that no held source places before August 30, 1945 (the formal proclamation of the war's end is not held), so it is a disclosed candidate that cannot be dated and not an end. A later general rule is not shown to have ended any command. Searches of the held corpus for \\\"Executive Order 9301\\\" and for the minimum-workweek wording found EO 9607 (the revocation) and EO 9332 (Solid Fuels Administration), which cites EO 9301 in a list of orders and does not revoke or amend it. The contents table of the held Federal Register issue of August 21, 1945 (10 FR page 10166) lists a rescission of the War Manpower Commission's regulations on the minimum wartime workweek; that page is not held, so the rescission's date and text cannot be read. It would concern regulations issued under section 3, not the order, and it does not name EO 9301's revocation, so it is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Section 3 gives the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission authority to issue regulations and set a different workweek; it is a delegation inside the order and ends with it. Section 5 is a rule of construction protecting other laws and agreements and has no force once the order is revoked. No other independent command is found.\",\"savings_check\":\"EO 9607 consists of the revocation sentence and no saving, exception or transition wording. Obligations that contractors incurred under contracts made while EO 9301 and the War Manpower Commission's regulations were in force arise from those contracts and the regulations, not from a continuing command of the order, and no held source shows any continuing effect; that is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.\",\"scope_check\":\"The inventory is five rows: the lead (authority recital and section 1) and sections 2 to 5. EO 10697 (22 FR 777, read in full) prescribed a complete new Tariff effective March 1, 1957 and in section 7 revoked EO 9591, so paragraph 1's clauses first ended 1957-03-01. 782ff84d9","path":"research/readiness/claims/claude-2026-10-18-codif-b2.jsonl","pointer":"line:15"}],"reported_material_gaps":[],"research_rationale":"EO 9789 of October 14, 1946 (official text 11 FR 11981, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line, F.R. Doc. 46-18658) establishes the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defines its functions in nine paragraphs; it takes effect October 14, 1946 (paragraph 9). The text is printed across columns interrupted by the issue's contents and codification guide, so paragraph 2 is inventoried in two quoted parts (before and after the interruption); no other text belongs to the order. EO 9788, signed the same day (F.R. Doc. 46-18657) and effective October 15, 1946, terminated the Office of Alien Property Custodian and moved its functions to the Attorney General; it is recorded as a later event on the clauses that direct the Custodian to act, because it changed who performed them without ending them. EO 9818 of January 7, 1947 (12 FR 133, read in full) re-issues the order with changes and in paragraph 9 provides 'This order supersedes Executive Order ... of October 14, 1946, entitled \"Establishing the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defining its functions.\"' (OCR prints the number '928.9'; the date and title identify EO 9789). EO 9818 states no effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1947-01-07. This resolves the draft's undated-ending conflict. No earlier end was found: EO 9789 has no expiry or condition, no evidence shows any directive was fully performed before supersession, and the OFR catalog, the saved-text corpus and the U.S. Code/eCFR hits (historical notes) show no other event. All clauses first ended 1947-01-07, the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text, not compared with page images.","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para1-establishes-administration"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para2-vests-functions-part1"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para2-vests-functions-part2"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para3-transfer-philippine-property"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para4-consult-secretary-of-state"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para5-transfer-personnel-records-funds"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para6-expenses-from-vested-funds"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para7-amends-eo9142-litigation"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para8-no-challenge-to-custodian-actions"},{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:9789#para9-effective-october-14-1946"}],"source_pins":[]}]}
